translation_en: Isma‘il narrated to us: Malik narrated to me, from Ishaq ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn Abi Talhah, that he heard Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, say: Abu Talhah had more date palms than any of the Ansar in Madinah. The most beloved of his possessions to him was Bayruha’, which faced the mosque. The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, used to enter it and drink from its pleasant water. When the verse, ‘You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love’ (3:92), was revealed, Abu Talhah stood and said, ‘Messenger of Allah, Allah says, “You will never attain righteousness until you spend from what you love” (3:92). The most beloved of my possessions to me is Bayruha’. It is charity for Allah, and I hope for its goodness and its store of reward with Allah. So place it, Messenger of Allah, wherever Allah shows you.’ The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Well done! That is a profitable possession; that is a profitable possession. I have heard what you said, and I think you should give it to your closest relatives.’ Abu Talhah said, ‘I will do that, Messenger of Allah.’ Abu Talhah then divided it among his relatives and his paternal cousins. ‘Abd Allah ibn Yusuf and Rawh ibn ‘Ubadah said, ‘That is a profit-bearing possession.’ Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to me, saying: I read to Malik, ‘A profitable possession.’

Muhammad ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Ansari narrated to us: My father narrated to me, from Thumamah, from Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: He gave it to Hassan and Ubayy, although I was closer to him, and he gave me none of it.

Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to me: Abu Damrah narrated to us: Musa ibn ‘Uqbah narrated to us, from Nafi‘, from ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Jews brought to the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, a man and a woman from among them who had committed adultery. He asked them, ‘What do you do with someone among you who commits adultery?’ They said, ‘We blacken their faces and beat them.’ He said, ‘Do you not find stoning in the Torah?’ They said, ‘We find nothing in it.’ ‘Abd Allah ibn Salam said to them, ‘You have lied. Bring the Torah and recite it, if you are truthful’ (3:93). Their Torah scholar, who taught it to them, placed his hand over the verse about stoning and began reading what was before and after his hand, but he did not read the verse about stoning. He moved his hand away from the verse about stoning, and the Prophet said, ‘What is this?’ When they saw that, they said, ‘It is the verse about stoning.’ He ordered that the two be stoned near the place where the funeral biers were by the mosque. I saw the man bend over the woman, shielding her from the stones.

Muhammad ibn Yusuf narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Maysarah, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, concerning the verse, ‘You are the best community brought forth for mankind’ (3:110). He said: They are the best of people for mankind; you bring them with chains around their necks until they enter Islam.

‘Ali ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, saying: ‘Amr said, ‘I heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: “When two groups among you were about to lose heart, though Allah was their protector” (3:122) was revealed concerning us. He said: We were the two groups, Banu Harithah and Banu Salimah. We would not like—or Sufyan once said, ‘It would not please me’—for it not to have been revealed, because Allah says, ‘though Allah was their protector’ (3:122).’

Hibban ibn Musa narrated to us: ‘Abd Allah informed us: Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Salim narrated to me, from his father, that he heard the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, when he raised his head from bowing in the final unit of the dawn prayer, say, after saying, ‘Allah hears whoever praises Him; our Lord, to You belongs all praise’: ‘O Allah, curse so-and-so, so-and-so, and so-and-so.’ Then Allah revealed, ‘You have no part in the matter…’ through His words, ‘for indeed, they are wrongdoers’ (3:128). Ishaq ibn Rashid also narrated it from al-Zuhri.

Musa ibn Isma‘il narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa‘d narrated to us: Ibn Shihab narrated to us, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyib and Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that when the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, wanted to supplicate against someone or for someone, he would perform the qunut supplication after bowing. Sometimes, after saying, ‘Allah hears whoever praises Him; O Allah, our Lord, to You belongs all praise,’ he would say, ‘O Allah, rescue al-Walid ibn al-Walid, Salamah ibn Hisham, and ‘Ayyash ibn Abi Rabi‘ah. O Allah, intensify Your punishment upon Mudar and make it years like the years of Yusuf.’ He would say this aloud. During some of his prayers, in the dawn prayer, he would say, ‘O Allah, curse so-and-so and so-and-so,’ referring to clans among the Arabs, until Allah revealed the verse, ‘You have no part in the matter…’ (3:128).

‘Amr ibn Khalid narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Abu Ishaq narrated to us, saying: I heard al-Bara’ ibn ‘Azib, may Allah be pleased with them both, say: On the day of Uhud, the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, appointed ‘Abd Allah ibn Jubayr over the infantry. They turned and fled, and that was when the Messenger was calling them from their rear. No one remained with the Prophet, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, except 12 men.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman Abu Ya‘qub narrated to us: Husayn ibn Muhammad narrated to us: Shayban narrated to us, from Qatadah: Anas narrated to us that Abu Talhah said: Drowsiness overcame us while we were in our ranks on the day of Uhud. He said: My sword kept falling from my hand, and I would pick it up; then it would fall, and I would pick it up.

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us—I think he said—Abu Bakr narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn ‘Abbas, concerning the verse, ‘Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs’ (3:173). He said: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, said it when he was thrown into the fire, and Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said it when people said, ‘The people have gathered against you, so fear them,’ but that increased them in faith, and they said, ‘Allah is sufficient for us, and He is the best disposer of affairs’ (3:173).

Malik ibn Isma‘il narrated to us: Isra’il narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Abu al-Duha, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: Ibrahim’s final words when he was thrown into the fire were, ‘Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best disposer of affairs.’

‘Abd Allah ibn Munir narrated to me; he heard Abu al-Nadr: ‘Abd al-Rahman—namely, the son of ‘Abd Allah ibn Dinar—narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Salih, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, said, ‘Whoever is given wealth by Allah but does not pay its zakat, his wealth will be made to appear to him on the Day of Resurrection as a bald-headed male serpent with two black marks above its eyes. It will encircle him and seize him by the sides of his mouth, saying, “I am your wealth; I am your treasure.”’ Then he recited this verse: ‘Those who are stingy with what Allah has given them from His bounty must not think…’ through the end of the verse (3:180).
